overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the hearing and chair-authority complaints fall outside the OML, and the evidence did not show deliberation outside a posted meeting on the water park.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Commission made a determination on the water park without holding a public hearing.
allegations.key_passage: We note first that the Division enforces the Open Meeting Law, and not separate laws that may require or govern the conduct of public hearings specifically.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Chair made a unilateral decision that shocked his board, allowing a soft opening of the water park.
allegations.key_passage: We also note that the Open Meeting Law does not govern the authority of individual public body members to act on behalf of the public body; thus, we do not review the allegation that the Chair made a unilateral decision, purportedly on behalf of the Commission.

allegations.summary: Alleged that the Commission deliberated outside a properly noticed meeting about the East Beach water park before its July 16 vote.
allegations.key_passage: we do not find sufficient evidence to support the allegation that the Commission deliberated outside of a properly noticed meeting regarding the water park.
